assignments.name: prompt
assignments.value:
=Review merge request !{{ $node["Extract MR Info"].json.mr_iid }} (`glab mr view {{ $node["Extract MR Info"].json.mr_iid }} --hostname gitlab-webservice-default.gitlab.svc.cluster.local`, diff via `glab mr diff {{ $node["Extract MR Info"].json.mr_iid }} --hostname gitlab-webservice-default.gitlab.svc.cluster.local`) against the pseudocode spec the developer was given — fetch `openspec/<task-slug>.md` from the MR's source branch (`glab api projects/{{ $env.GITLAB_PROJECT_PATH }}/repository/files/openspec%2F<task-slug>.md/raw?ref={{ $node["Extract MR Info"].json.source_branch }} --hostname gitlab-webservice-default.gitlab.svc.cluster.local`, URL-encode the slug; list `openspec/` on that branch first if you don't know the exact filename). Check: does the diff actually implement what the spec describes (not just something plausible-looking), is there test coverage for the changed logic, does it follow this repo's existing conventions (see AGENTS.md), and does it avoid obvious correctness bugs. Do NOT check CI/pipeline status yourself — that is handled separately in parallel, your review is code-against-spec only.

Output your verdict as the FIRST line of your response, exactly `APPROVE` or `REQUEST_CHANGES` (nothing else on that line), followed by your notes. If REQUEST_CHANGES, the notes MUST name the specific file(s)/function(s) and what's wrong or missing — "needs improvement" alone is not acceptable feedback, the developer re-reading this has no other context. Then, regardless of verdict, leave that same verdict + notes as a comment on Taiga task {{ $node["Extract MR Info"].json.task_iid }} so the developer sees it where they already work: `GET $TAIGA_URL/api/v1/tasks/{{ $node["Extract MR Info"].json.task_iid }}` for its current `version`, then `PATCH $TAIGA_URL/api/v1/tasks/{{ $node["Extract MR Info"].json.task_iid }}` with `{"version": <version>, "comment": "TL review: <verdict>\n\n<notes>"}` (bearer `$TAIGA_TOKEN`).
